title: Kenya becomes independent
summary: Kenya became independent within the Commonwealth at midnight on 12 December 1963, when the Union Jack was lowered and the Kenyan flag raised at Uhuru Gardens in Nairobi. Jomo Kenyatta, held in the 1950s over the Mau Mau uprising and released in 1961, was prime minister; Kenya became a republic on 12 December 1964 with Kenyatta as first president.

uncertainty.note: Union Jack lowered on the night of 11-12 December; new flag raised at midnight.

where.modern_name: Uhuru Gardens National Monument, Lang'ata Road, Nairobi, Kenya
where.historical_name: Nairobi, capital of the colony of Kenya becoming an independent state

importance.justification: Kenya gained independence after the Mau Mau uprising and the 1950s state of emergency.

related.because: EBSCO places the Mau Mau uprising in 1952-1957 with the emergency lifted in 1960, followed by Kenyatta, convicted over Mau Mau in 1953 and released in 1961, leading Kenya to independence in 1963.

sources.title: U.S. Relations with Kenya
sources.publisher: Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State

reviewer_note: Another web account places the flag-raising at Uhuru Park; the summary follows the Citizen Guide (Uhuru Gardens). The prime-minister title comes from the State Department page; Kenyatta's release in 1961 and 1953 conviction from EBSCO; the 1964 republic date from the Citizen Guide.
